claims.claim_text: The indexed Preston E. James is the University of Michigan geographer who led the COI Latin-American Section and later served in OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact distinctive name, lieutenant-colonel rank, university title, Latin-American specialization, and COI role align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; full name, middle initial, rank, profession, and unusually specific wartime assignment corroborate the match.
claims.temporal_assessment: A contemporary 1942 source places James at COI while retaining his Michigan faculty title.
claims.match_notes: The Box 369 personnel file remains unreviewed; the private service number is not reproduced.

claims.claim_text: Preston James's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was the Office of the Coordinator of Information, where he headed the Latin-American Section.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A contemporary review identifies James as COI section chief; NARA records that remaining COI units became OSS on June 13, 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; exact name, specialization, university title, and wartime role align.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit administrative succession from COI to OSS.
claims.match_notes: COI is a government assignment, not a civilian employer.

claims.claim_text: Preston James's last civilian employer before COI and OSS was the University of Michigan, where he was Professor of Geography.

claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence; exact name, discipline, Latin-American specialization, and COI role form a specific match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicit faculty-to-COI sequence; the faculty appointment may have continued while he served in Washington.
claims.match_notes: The exact leave or separation terms require Michigan or personnel-file review.
